clinician.trajectory_summary: A 32-month-old male presented with pruritus, generalized erythema, follicular papules, and progressive non-painful desquamative exanthem on hands, feet, genitalia, and periorificial areas. Initial differential diagnoses included urticaria and Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome (SSSS). During hospitalization, the patient showed a clinically favorable evolution with slight improvement. On hospital day 7, a dermatologist described diffuse erythematosquamous plaques of cephalocaudal evolution, follicular hyperkeratosis, palmoplantar keratoderma, and areas of healthy skin. Oxacillin was withdrawn, and treatment with glycerin soap, rehydrating cream, cetirizine, and prednisolone was initiated. Other conditions like psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis were ruled out. At 14-day follow-up, clinical improvement was noted, though erythematous lesions persisted. By 3-month follow-up, there was complete clinical resolution of the dermatological problems.
